summary: inventory-api is running as an enabled OpenRC service on TCP 8080. batchworker has a persistent 128 MiB hard and soft per-process virtual-memory limit. Failed oversized allocations did not interrupt the API, including after reboot. Alpine 3.23 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts were retained.
actions_performed: Created unprivileged inventoryapi and batchworker accounts.
Implemented inventory-api using installed socat and a POSIX shell handler.
Enabled inventory-api in the OpenRC default runlevel.
Applied a 131072 KiB RLIMIT_AS to batchworker through a root-owned login shell wrapper and PAM limits configuration.
Tested oversized batch allocations and API isolation.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified persistence and recovery.

evidence.summary: OpenRC reports the service started and enabled; socat listens on 0.0.0.0:8080; /health and /inventory return valid JSON over NODE_IP before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: batchworker limited to 128 MB virtual memory per process
evidence.summary: Direct batchworker sessions report soft and hard virtual-memory limits of 131072 KiB before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Failed batch allocation does not interrupt the API
evidence.summary: Oversized allocations failed with 'awk: out of memory'; the API PID remained unchanged and health responses stayed OK before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel retained
evidence.summary: Both baselines report Alpine Linux v3.23 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 84abd555-6a78-4d98-920a-5a2667ff58e2; reboot acknowledgement was captured; node returned with boot ID 61a27240-f268-4875-939e-747b030a07cb; service, listener, API data, worker limits, and identical configuration digest recovered, followed by a successful post-reboot isolation test.
